summary: ARES-IV Tactical Martian Map is an integrated surface navigation, hazard-mapping, and mission-control system built for astronauts conducting Marswalks across the entire Martian surface. By fusing orbital NASA Mars Trek imagery and AI4Mars terrain classification with live aerial Intel RealSense D415 RGB-D reconnaissance, autonomous A* and Dijkstra pathfinding, and resilient ESP32 mesh backups, the platform closes the gap between coarse orbital maps and meter-scale surface hazards—keeping explorers safe across diverse global terrains including crater walls, steep slopes, rock fields, and communication blackouts.
details:
ARES-IV Tactical Martian Map is a decentralized, hardware-in-the-loop surface navigation, 3D hazard-mapping, and mission-control ecosystem designed to keep astronauts safe during Extravehicular Activities (Marswalks) across the Martian surface without relying on Earth. Traditionally, planetary navigation studies orbital maps and surface telemetry in isolation while depending on Earth Mission Control, leaving explorers vulnerable to the 3-to-22-minute Earth-Mars communication latency, meter scale hazards hidden beneath dust, local communication blackouts, and the severe mobility and downward visibility constraints of heavy, pressurized planetary spacesuits. Our platform uniquely fuses global orbital intelligence with live aerial 3D depth reconnaissance and wearable biometric telemetry to provide instant, life-saving autonomy in the field.

How it works:

ARES-IV ingests multi-layered NASA planetary datasets—dynamically blending Mars Trek global color and thermal mosaics (Viking MDIM 2.1 and THEMIS Day IR), MOLA and HiRISE elevation and slope models, MSL REMS and Perseverance MEDA/RAD environmental baselines, and NASA JPL AI4Mars terrain traversability classes (soil, bedrock, sand, and big rock). To close the gap between coarse orbital maps and restricted spacesuit downward visibility, a physical scout drone deploys from a scale mother rover carrying a nadir-pointing (-90°) Intel RealSense D415 active infrared depth camera.

An embedded Rust telemetry link validates radio-frequency health at 10 Hz and streams SHA-256 verified captures to our Python 3D vision engine, which executes RANSAC + SVD ground-plane fitting, DBSCAN boulder and crevice clustering, persistent Log-Odds occupancy mapping, and cached A* and Dijkstra optimal pathfinding at ~30 FPS. Simultaneously, wearable microcontroller hardware monitors spacesuit life-support biometrics (oxygen pressure, heart rate, radiation dose, battery, and 6-DOF IMU step odometry). If an oxygen leak drops reserves below 15 minutes or crater walls block line-of-sight to the Base Station for more than 0.8 seconds, the system triggers an immediate emergency return vector route and automatically fails over to an ESP32 satellite mesh that persists compact route payloads onto physical MicroSD storage.

Key Benefits & Impact:

  • Eliminates dependency on Earth Mission Control during time-critical EVA emergencies where 3-to-22-minute communication delays are inoperable.
  • Protects astronauts in rigid, heavy spacesuits from trip and puncture hazards by acting as aerial "downward eyes" that detect knee-high boulders, crevices, and steep inclines.
  • Preserves spacesuit oxygen and metabolic reserves by routing explorers around energy-draining sand traps and hazardous slopes using AI4Mars cost classes.
  • Guarantees continuous navigation during communication blackouts through sub-second (0.8 s) failover to an ESP32 satellite mesh with physical storage route backups.
  • Offers a modular, hardware-validated architecture directly transferable to NASA's Artemis lunar program and future crewed Mars missions.
  • Supports NASA mission planners in designing safe surface corridors, scheduling scientific survey stops, and validating autonomous systems for Artemis lunar and future Mars missions.

Tools & Technologies:

  • React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet & Three.js: Full-stack Mission Control web dashboard and interactive 2D/3D Martian cartography.
  • React Native & Expo Go (iPad 11"): Glove-friendly astronaut EVA field terminal displaying live camera feeds, hazard maps, biometric gauges, and one-tap emergency return routes.
  • Python (OpenCV, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch/SAM, pyrealsense2): Real-time 3D perception pipeline, RANSAC + SVD plane fitting, DBSCAN obstacle clustering, Log-Odds mapping, and A*/Dijkstra pathfinding.
  • Rust (DRON-LINK): High-reliability drone-to-ground telemetry, 10 Hz RF link validation (RTT, RFC 3550 jitter, RSSI, packet loss), and SHA-256 file synchronization.
  • C/C++, PlatformIO & painlessMesh (ESP32 / ESP32-S3): Autonomous hardware nodes for the orbital satellite, base habitat, EVA space suit biometrics (6-DOF IMU), and FAT32 MicroSD route backup mesh.
  • Scout Drone, Intel RealSense D415, Raspberry Pi 3 & Scale Mother Rover: Tangible hardware-in-the-loop reconnaissance and command ecosystem.

Creative Elements:

  • Built as a 100% tangible, hardware in the loop tabletop ecosystem combining a real scout drone, a physical mother rover with a deployment bay, and biometric nodes instead of relying solely on software simulations.
  • Connects planetary orbital data directly to human spacesuit biomechanics by pairing nadir 3D depth vision with live suit oxygen and heart rate contingency alerts.
  • Features a predictive Command Center that caches surrounding terrain quadrants, automatically requests drone sweeps into unmapped areas, and operates 100% offline.
